name: Applied AI and Solutions Engineering
guide:
Applied AI and Solutions Engineering is customer-facing technical work, the job that sits between a finished AI product and the team that has to run it in production. In our data the postings read like forward-deployed engineer, applied AI architect, applied AI engineer, and applied AI transformation manager, and the common thread is hands-on implementation work done with or for a customer. People in this seat sit on calls, work inside a client's codebase, and get a model or an agent talking to real data and real workflows. That is different from Machine Learning Engineering, which mostly builds and trains models inside the company and rarely owns a single customer relationship. It is also different from AI Product and Program Management, which decides what gets built and when, but does not write the integration code or carry a support escalation to resolution.

Degrees matter less here than in research-heavy machine learning roles, and most of the postings we pulled describe required skills rather than a required diploma. A computer science or engineering degree still opens doors, especially at large employers like OpenAI, Databricks, and Anthropic, but it reads as a preference rather than a hard filter in this sample. We did not find a specific vendor certification, such as an AWS or Databricks certification, named as a requirement across the postings we queried, so we are not going to invent one here. What the postings ask for instead is proof of hands-on capability, often demonstrated through take-home projects, portfolio work, or prior customer-facing engineering experience. If a certification does appear in a listing you are reading, treat it as a plus rather than a gate.

Of the 293 postings we have on file for this category, 175 are tagged mid-level, 42 senior, 38 manager, 21 staff, and smaller numbers at principal, lead, director, and intern. That spread tells you this is mostly a mid-career role, not an entry-level one, and most companies want someone who has already shipped software or supported customers technically before moving into applied AI. Junior candidates tend to get in through an adjacent path, often support engineering, backend engineering, or data science, rather than starting directly in this title. Senior and staff postings ask for a track record of owning a technical relationship end to end, from scoping through deployment to renewal conversations. Management-level postings, tagged manager or director in our data, ask for people who have already done the individual-contributor version of this job.

The skills most frequently listed across these postings are Rust, AWS, and large language models, followed closely by Python, Scala, GCP, and Azure, so comfort across at least one major cloud and one or two production languages is closer to a baseline than a bonus. Model evaluation, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering appear often, alongside frameworks like LangChain and Hugging Face and infrastructure tools like Spark, Databricks, and Kubernetes. Java, JavaScript, and TypeScript also show up regularly, reflecting how much of this work is building integrations and internal tools rather than pure model development. Retrieval-augmented generation and MLOps appear in a meaningful minority of postings, which tracks with how much of the job is making an existing model work reliably against a customer's own data. PyTorch and SQL round out the list, useful for anyone who needs to debug a model's behavior or pull the data a customer is asking about.

Based on today's snapshot, we currently track approximately 179 open postings tagged Applied AI and Solutions Engineering, out of 293 total postings we have logged for this category. OpenAI, Databricks, and Anthropic post the most roles in this category by a wide margin, with Nebius, Cresta, Cognition, and SentinelOne also appearing repeatedly. Only 10 of the 293 postings in our database include an actual salary figure, and among those the range runs from $67,816 to $300,000 per year, clustering mostly between roughly $120,000 and $200,000. That small sample skews toward government and enterprise employers like Booz Allen Hamilton and NIST, which post pay bands more often than venture-backed AI labs do. Treat that range as directional rather than representative, since it covers only a small slice of the postings we track for this role.
